Sure! Here’s a simple yet flavorful way to make an **Indian‑style grilled steak** at home.  
The idea is to marinate the steak with aromatic spices, yogurt, lemon juice, and fresh herbs so it becomes tender and packed with classic North‑Indian flavors.

---

### Ingredients  

| Item | Quantity |
|------|----------|
| Ribeye / sirloin steak (1–2 lb) | 1 piece per person |
| Plain Greek yogurt | ½ cup |
| Lemon juice | 2 tbsp |
| Fresh ginger paste | 1 tsp |
| Garlic paste | 1 tsp |
| Ground cumin | 1 tsp |
| Ground coriander | 1 tsp |
| Garam masala | ½ tsp |
| Turmeric powder | ¼ tsp |
| Red chili flakes (optional) | ¼ tsp |
| Salt & pepper | to taste |
| Olive oil or melted butter | 1 tbsp |
| Fresh cilantro leaves | handful (for garnish) |

> *Tip:* If you’re short on time, use store‑bought “tandoori” spice mix instead – just add about 1 tablespoon plus some yogurt and lemon juice.

---

### Equipment  

* Grill pan or outdoor grill  
* Tongs  
* Small bowl for mixing the marinades  
* Plate lined with parchment paper (to catch drips)

---

### Instructions  

#### 1️⃣ Prep the Marinade  
In a small bowl combine:

```
• Yogurt + lemon juice → base
• Ginger paste + garlic paste → aromatics
• Cumin + coriander + garam masala + turmeric (+ chili if you want heat)
• Salt & pepper
• A splash of olive oil/melted butter (helps keep meat moist)
```

Whisk until smooth. Taste; adjust salt or spices as preferred.

#### 2️⃣ Marinate the Steak  
Pat the steak dry with paper towels. Place it in a shallow dish or zip‑lock bag, pour the mixture over it, making sure both sides get coated. Seal/cover and refrigerate for **at least 30 minutes**, ideally **up to 8 hours**—the longer, the more flavor!

If you’re pressed for time, even a quick 15‑minute soak will do wonders compared to plain grilling.

#### 3️⃣ Preheat Your Grill  
Heat your grill or skillet to high flame (~450°F). Let it sear quickly but don’t let it burn. Oil the grates lightly to prevent sticking.

#### 4️⃣ Cook the Steak  
Remove from fridge, pat off excess sauce (you’ll still have plenty left!). Season again with a pinch of salt.

Place steak on hot grill:
- **Medium‑rare:** ~5 min each side (120–125°F internal temp).
- **Medium:** ~7 min each side (140°F).

Use tongs only—avoid pinching the meat with a fork because that releases juices.

While grilling, brush a little extra yogurt‑spice mixture onto the surface once or twice—it adds moisture and keeps the crust juicy.

#### 5️⃣ Rest & Slice  
Let the cooked steak rest on a plate covered loosely with foil for **5–7 minutes**. This allows juices to redistribute.

Slice thinly against the grain. Serve immediately.

---

### Serving Ideas  

| Dish | How to Pair |
|------|-------------|
| Grilled naan bread | Warm it in a toaster oven or skillet |
| Mint raita | Mix yogurt, chopped mint, cucumber, salt |
| Sautéed onions & bell peppers | Quick stir‑fry in a dash of ghee |
| Roasted potatoes | Toss with cumin, paprika, and olive oil |
| Green salad | Light vinaigrette with lime juice |

A drizzle of **chutney** (like tamarind or mango) also gives a sweet‑sour contrast that works beautifully with the smoky steak.

---

### Quick FAQ  

| Question | Answer |
|-----------|--------|
| What cut? | Sirloin, ribeye, strip steak work best—they stay juicy when grilled. |
| Need no yogurt? | Use mayo or sour cream mixed with spices—but yogurt helps tenderize. |
| Vegetarian version? | Replace steak with paneer tikka or tofu cubes. |
| Leftovers? | Store in airtight container; reheat gently in a skillet or microwave. |

Enjoy your homemade Indian‑styled steak—a perfect blend of Western technique and Eastern zest!
